error: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
description: You are trying to run a Git command in a folder that is not a Git repository.
causes: You haven't initialized a Git repository in this folder.
You are in the wrong directory.
The .git folder was accidentally deleted.
fixes: Navigate to the correct project folder: cd your-project-folder
Initialize a new Git repository: git init
If you intended to clone a repo: git clone <repo-url>

description: You are trying to add a remote named 'origin', but one is already configured.
causes: A remote named 'origin' was already added previously.
You cloned the repository, which automatically sets up 'origin'.
fixes: View existing remotes: git remote -v
Update the existing remote URL: git remote set-url origin <new-url>
Remove and re-add origin: git remote remove origin && git remote add origin <url>

error: error: failed to push some refs to (rejected non-fast-forward)
description: Push rejected because the remote branch has commits you don't have locally.
causes: Someone else pushed changes to the remote branch.
You made changes directly on GitHub (like editing README).
Your local branch is behind the remote branch.
fixes: Pull the remote changes first: git pull origin main
If there are conflicts, resolve them, then commit and push again.
If you're sure you want to overwrite (dangerous!): git push --force origin main

description: Git found conflicting changes in the same part of a file during a merge or pull.
causes: Two branches modified the same lines in a file.
A remote change conflicts with your local change.
A rebase encountered conflicting edits.
fixes: Open the conflicting file and look for conflict markers: <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>>
Edit the file to keep the correct changes and remove the markers.
Stage the resolved file: git add <file>
Complete the merge: git commit

description: SSH authentication failed. Your SSH key is not configured or not recognized by GitHub.
causes: SSH keys are not generated on your machine.
Your SSH key is not added to your GitHub account.
The SSH agent is not running.
You're using the wrong SSH key.
fixes: Generate an SSH key: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Start the SSH agent: eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
Add your key to the agent: ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
Copy your public key and add it to GitHub Settings > SSH Keys
Test connection: ssh -T git@github.com
Alternative: Use HTTPS URL instead of SSH

description: Git could not verify your identity. Typically happens with HTTPS using wrong credentials.
causes: GitHub no longer accepts password authentication for HTTPS.
Your Personal Access Token (PAT) has expired.
Wrong username or token provided.
fixes: Generate a new Personal Access Token on GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Tokens
Use the token as your password when prompted.
Update stored credentials in your system's credential manager.
Consider switching to SSH authentication.

error: error: src refspec main does not match any
description: You're trying to push to a branch that doesn't exist locally, usually because no commits have been made.
causes: You haven't made any commits yet.
The branch name is wrong (e.g., 'main' vs 'master').
The repository was just initialized without any files.
fixes: Make sure you have at least one commit: git add . && git commit -m "Initial commit"
Check your current branch name: git branch
If the branch is 'master', push to master: git push origin master
Rename branch if needed: git branch -M main

error: error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge
description: Git is preventing a merge or checkout because you have uncommitted changes that would be lost.
causes: You have modified files that conflict with incoming changes.
Uncommitted work exists that hasn't been saved.
fixes: Option 1: Save changes with stash: git stash, then pull/merge, then git stash pop
Option 2: Commit your changes: git add . && git commit -m "Save work"
Option 3: Discard local changes (destructive): git checkout -- <file>
